B1:
Touched fires many times per step contact (every body part, every physics contact frame) before Destroy() replicates/completes, and there's no debounce, so several handlers run in the same moment and each adds 10. Destroy also happens after awarding, but other queued Touched events still run (deferred signals).
Fix: add a server-side guard that flips before awarding:
```lua
local part = script.Parent
local collected = false
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
  if collected then return end
  local char = hit:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
  local plr = char and game.Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(char)
  if not plr then return end
  collected = true
  part.CanTouch = false
  plr.leaderstats.Coins.Value += 10
  part:Destroy()
end)
```
For respawning coins, use a per-player debounce table or a cooldown instead of Destroy.
B2:
With StreamingEnabled, the client only has parts near the player; far-away doors (and possibly their Hotel/Buildings models) haven't streamed in at script start, so direct indexing errors. They can also stream out later.
Fixes:
1) Wait: `local door = workspace.Map.Buildings.Hotel:WaitForChild("Door", 10)` (each level with WaitForChild + timeout) and set the Hotel/door model ModelStreamingMode = Atomic (or Persistent for something always needed) so the whole model arrives together.
2) Better for many doors: tag doors with CollectionService ("Door") and use CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal("Door") + GetTagged to connect when each door streams in (and GetInstanceRemovedSignal to clean up). Alternatively do door touch logic on the server, which always has everything.
(Persistent / Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync are also options, but don't turn streaming off.)
B3:
Bugs:
1) Ignores the pcall result: returns PurchaseGranted even if GetAsync/SetAsync failed -> charged, nothing received.
2) No PurchaseId idempotency: Roblox can redeliver the same receipt (timeouts, retries, server shutdown) -> double coins.
3) plr may be nil (player left) -> plr.UserId errors inside pcall -> swallowed, then PurchaseGranted -> charged, nothing.
4) GetAsync + SetAsync is a non-atomic read-modify-write; concurrent writes (another server, autosave) overwrite each other; should use UpdateAsync, and coins should go into the player's session data, not a separate store.
5) Doesn't check ProductId.
Correct behaviour: look up the player; if absent return NotProcessedYet. Check the product. In one UpdateAsync on the player's data, if PurchaseId already in receipts list return unchanged; else add coins and record PurchaseId. Only if that save succeeded return PurchaseGranted; on any error return NotProcessedYet. Assign ProcessReceipt once.
B4:
Remote arguments are serialized: metatables (and functions) are not sent, so the client gets a plain table {Name="Rifle", Ammo=30} without Weapon methods -> w:Fire() is nil. Instances are sent as references, and the client can't see ServerStorage contents (never replicated), so the Muzzle reference arrives as nil.
Fix: send plain data (e.g. {Name, Ammo} or an id) and reconstruct on the client: `local w = setmetatable(data, Weapon)` using a shared Weapon module in ReplicatedStorage. For the part, put it where clients can see it (ReplicatedStorage or workspace) and send the reference or just its name/id, or clone it into a replicated location before firing (and wait until it exists client-side).
B5:
workspace:Raycast's second argument is a direction vector whose length is the ray length. `.Unit` makes it 1 stud long, so the ray stops 1 stud from the origin. It also likely hits the shooter's own character/tool, since there's no RaycastParams filter.
Fix:
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {shooterCharacter}
local MAX_RANGE = 300
local dir = (target - origin).Unit * MAX_RANGE
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if r then print(r.Instance, r.Position) end
```
(Or use `target - origin` directly to stop exactly at the target, guarding against zero-length vectors.)
B6:
When the last player leaves, the server shuts down right away (or it's closing for an update). PlayerRemoving fires, but the server doesn't wait for your yielding SetAsync to finish, so the save is cut off and lost. Blind SetAsync can also overwrite newer data.
Standard fix: game:BindToClose(function() ... end) that saves every player's data in parallel (task.spawn per player) and waits until all saves finish or ~25 s pass (engine gives ~30 s). Make saves per-player serialized/idempotent (PlayerRemoving and BindToClose may both save the same profile; track in-flight saves), use UpdateAsync with session-lock release, add periodic autosaves (60-180 s) so little is lost anyway, and skip the long wait in Studio (RunService:IsStudio()).
B7:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local UseAbility = game.ReplicatedStorage.Remotes.UseAbility
local COOLDOWN = 2
local lastUse: {[Player]: number} = {}

UseAbility.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, abilityId)
  if typeof(abilityId) ~= "string" then return end
  local now = os.clock()
  local last = lastUse[player]
  if last and now - last < COOLDOWN then return end -- silently ignore spam
  lastUse[player] = now
  local char = player.Character
  local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  performAbility(player, abilityId) -- server-side validation of range/targets
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
  lastUse[player] = nil -- no leak
end)
```
Cooldown timestamp set before any yield so spam can't slip through; server clock only; table cleared on leave.
B8:
```lua
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local DSS = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local store = DSS:GetDataStore("PlayerData")
local GEMS100 = 123456
local inFlight = {}

local handlers = {[GEMS100] = function(data) data.Gems = (data.Gems or 0) + 100 end}

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  local handler = handlers[info.ProductId]
  if not handler then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  if inFlight[info.PurchaseId] then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  inFlight[info.PurchaseId] = true
  local ok, err = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, "player_"..info.PlayerId, function(data)
    data = data or {Gems = 0, Receipts = {}}
    data.Receipts = data.Receipts or {}
    if data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return data end -- already granted
    handler(data)
    data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = os.time() -- prune to newest ~100
    return data
  end)
  inFlight[info.PurchaseId] = nil
  if not ok then warn(err) return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  -- update live session/leaderstats from saved data here
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
```
Assign once; grant + PurchaseId marker in the same atomic write; PurchaseGranted only after a successful save. If you use a session-locked profile, write into it and force-save instead of a separate UpdateAsync.
B9:
```lua
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.4, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local SHOWN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0)
local HIDDEN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1.5, 0)
local current

local function open()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  menu.Position = HIDDEN
  menu.Visible = true
  current = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = SHOWN})
  current:Play()
end

local function close()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  local t = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = HIDDEN})
  current = t
  t.Completed:Connect(function(state)
    if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and current == t then
      menu.Visible = false
    end
  end)
  t:Play()
end
```
(AnchorPoint should be 0.5,0.5 for centering.) Visible is only cleared after the slide-out completes, and a re-open cancels the pending hide.
B10:
```lua
local MAX_RANGE, DAMAGE = 200, 20

local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
  if typeof(targetPos) ~= "Vector3" or targetPos ~= targetPos then return end
  local char = player.Character
  local head = char and char:FindFirstChild("Head")
  local myHum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not head or not myHum or myHum.Health <= 0 then return end
  local origin = head.Position
  local offset = targetPos - origin
  if offset.Magnitude < 1e-3 then return end
  local params = RaycastParams.new()
  params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {char}
  local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, offset.Unit * MAX_RANGE, params)
  if not result then return end
  local model = result.Instance:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
  local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if hum and hum.Health > 0 then
    hum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE)
  end
end
```
Add a fire-rate cooldown when calling this from a remote; the server computes range from its own head position.

```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local TAG = "KillBrick"
local conns: {[BasePart]: RBXScriptConnection} = {}

local function onAdded(part)

  conns[part] = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)

local function onRemoved(part)

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TAG):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TAG):Connect(onRemoved)
```

B12:
```lua
local TeleportService = game:GetService("TeleportService")
local MAX_ATTEMPTS, BASE_DELAY = 5, 1

local function safeTeleport(placeId: number, players: {Player}, teleportData)
  local options = Instance.new("TeleportOptions")
  if teleportData then options:SetTeleportData(teleportData) end
  local attempt = 0
  local ok, result
  repeat
    attempt += 1
    ok, result = pcall(TeleportService.TeleportAsync, TeleportService, placeId, players, options)
    if not ok then task.wait(BASE_DELAY * 2 ^ (attempt - 1)) end
  until ok or attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS
  if not ok then warn("Teleport failed:", result) end
  return ok, result
end

TeleportService.TeleportInitFailed:Connect(function(player, result, errorMessage, placeId, options)
  if result == Enum.TeleportResult.IsTeleporting or result == Enum.TeleportResult.Unauthorized then return end
  warn(player.Name, "teleport init failed:", result, errorMessage)
  task.delay(BASE_DELAY, function()
    if player.Parent then safeTeleport(placeId, {player}, options and options:GetTeleportData()) end
  end)
end)
```
pcall catches immediate errors; TeleportInitFailed catches failures after the call succeeded (per player). Cap retries in real code (track per-player attempt count) and only pass non-sensitive teleportData.
B13:
(a) Buy: client -> server RemoteEvent (e.g. BuySword) carrying only the item id (or a client->server RemoteFunction if the UI wants a success/fail reply). The server owns the balance (session data) and does all validation: item exists, price from server catalog, enough coins, rate limit; it deducts and grants.
(b) Coin counter: server -> client. Easiest is replication: leaderstats IntValue or a player attribute (player:SetAttribute("Coins", n)) the UI listens to via GetAttributeChangedSignal/Changed; or a server->client RemoteEvent (FireClient) with the new balance.
Why not server->client RemoteFunction (InvokeClient): the server yields until the client answers; a malicious/laggy client can never return, error, or disconnect, hanging the server thread forever (or erroring); the client's return value is untrustworthy anyway. The UI update is a one-way notification, so a RemoteEvent or replicated value is correct. The client display is cosmetic only.
B14:
Teleport data (TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData / GetJoinData().TeleportData): convenient, arrives with the player, but it's client-visible and passes through the client, so it can be tampered with; it's lost if the teleport fails or the player joins the place directly; size-limited. Fine for non-authoritative things like the chosen loadout id, map, party/match id.
DataStores: authoritative, persistent, server-only; coin balance belongs here (session-locked profile saved before teleport, loaded in the match place). Must handle save-before-load ordering (session lock / wait for release) and budget limits.
MemoryStores: fast, server-only, expiring shared memory across servers - good for short-lived handoff state (match assignment, reserved loadout, queue) with a TTL, not as permanent storage.
Choice: keep coins in the DataStore player profile (session locking, save on leave/teleport, load in destination); pass loadout as teleport data only as a hint, validated on the destination server against owned items (or store the selection in the profile/MemoryStore keyed by userId). Never trust coin values from teleport data.
B15:
Per-instance Scripts (610 copies): duplicated code that drifts out of sync, hard to update/fix, more memory and script start-up cost, many connections/loops, and copies break when streamed or cloned at runtime.
Tag-driven: tag instances with CollectionService (Door, Pickup, Turret) and have one server Script/ModuleScript per system (DoorSystem, PickupSystem, TurretSystem). Each system does: for _, inst in GetTagged(tag) do setup(inst) end, plus GetInstanceAddedSignal(tag) for runtime-spawned or (client side) streamed-in instances, and GetInstanceRemovedSignal(tag) to disconnect and clear state (also fires when instances stream out/are destroyed). Per-instance state lives in a table keyed by instance (or attributes for config, e.g. door speed, turret range). Turrets are updated by one central Heartbeat loop over active turrets (with distance/LOD culling) instead of 60 loops. Server owns logic/security; client systems handle visuals using the same tag signals, which is what makes streaming work. Optional: use a component framework pattern (Component module per tag).
B16:
Ownership: give the driver network ownership of the car (VehicleSeat / server sets primaryPart:SetNetworkOwner(driverPlayer) when they sit; set back to nil/server or auto when they leave). This gives responsive, lag-free driving physics; server-owned cars feel laggy to the driver.
Risk: the owning client simulates the car's physics and the server accepts its positions, so an exploiter can teleport, speed-hack, fly or fling the car (and use it to fling others), and fake lap/checkpoint progress.
Server must still validate: the driver actually occupies the seat; speed/acceleration caps against car stats (sample positions over time); no teleports/impossible displacement; checkpoints passed in order with plausible times; lap/finish times computed by the server, not reported by the client; collisions/damage and rewards decided server-side. On violation, reset the car or take ownership back (SetNetworkOwner(nil)). Remove ownership when the driver exits, and don't trust any client remote for race results.
B17:
Use an UnreliableRemoteEvent for the aim/position stream (and keep a reliable RemoteEvent for discrete state changes like fire start/stop, reload, hits).
Constraints: best-effort - packets can be dropped (network loss, payload > ~1,000 bytes, throttling, no handler connected) and are not ordered; no yield on send.
Handling: keep payloads tiny (a few numbers - e.g. compressed direction/position, buffer or quantized values, no instances/tables); include a sequence number or timestamp and ignore older packets (latest-wins); treat each packet as full current state, not a delta, so drops don't matter; interpolate on receivers; reduce rate (e.g. 10-20 Hz) or send only when aim changes significantly; validate on the server (type, NaN/inf, rate per player, position plausibility vs. server character). Important one-off events must never go over the unreliable channel. Also consider that position already replicates via physics - often only aim needs sending.
B18:
Split NPCs across several Actors (e.g. 8-16 Actor instances, each with a Script handling a subset of NPC ids; not one Actor and not 200). In each worker, run the expensive read-only work in parallel: RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel(fn) (or Actor:BindToMessageParallel), do raycasts (workspace:Raycast works in parallel), distance checks and path scoring, store results locally, then task.synchronize() and apply results (set CFrames, Humanoid:MoveTo, fire events) in serial. Throttle: not every NPC every frame.
Limitations:
- In the parallel phase you can't create/destroy/reparent instances or write most properties (non-thread-safe members error "not safe in parallel"); reads and spatial queries are fine.
- Each Actor is its own Luau VM: module state isn't shared; require modules in serial at load; communicate via Actor:SendMessage (args copied) or SharedTable (SharedTableRegistry; atomic updates, no functions/Instance keys).
- Scripts must be descendants of the Actor; instances modified should be under that Actor.
- Overhead of sync/messaging can exceed gains for small work; measure with the MicroProfiler. Pathfinding (PathfindingService) yields and isn't parallel-safe - compute paths in serial/occasionally.
B19:
Workspace: StreamingEnabled = true (must be set in Studio, not script). Sensible settings: StreamingMinRadius ~64 (default), StreamingTargetRadius ~1024 default (lower, e.g. 256-512, for mobile-heavy games), StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic, StreamingIntegrityMode = PauseOutsideLoadedArea (or MinimumRadiusPause), ModelStreamingBehavior = Improved. Per model: ModelStreamingMode = Atomic for buildings/interactables that must arrive whole, Persistent only for small essentials (spawn, key objects), Nonatomic default for scenery. Use low-detail StreamingMeshes/LOD for distant landmarks (LevelOfDetail = StreamingMesh).
Scripts: client scripts can no longer assume parts exist - replace direct indexing with WaitForChild (with timeouts) on Atomic models, or better CollectionService tag added/removed signals to set up and clean up as things stream in/out; nil-check everything. Server: before teleporting a player, call Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(pos). Server code still sees everything. Test with low radii in Studio to catch bugs; don't turn streaming off to fix them.
B20:
Cause: 80 players x 1 save / 5 s = ~960 writes/min, in bursts on the same tick. Even within the experience budget (write 300 + 20 x CCU/min, plus per-server limits ~60 + 40 x players), bursts overflow the DataStore request queue (30 requests per queue); queued calls wait and then fail with queue-full errors (301-306, e.g. 302), so saves are dropped. Blind SetAsync also overwrites newer data and doesn't protect against other servers.
Better design:
- Keep data in a server session cache; mark dirty on change.
- Autosave every 60-180 s, staggered with a random per-player offset, only if dirty.
- Save on PlayerRemoving (releasing the session lock) and in BindToClose (all players in parallel, ~25 s deadline).
- Use UpdateAsync with a session lock instead of SetAsync.
- Check GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before saving; on failure retry with exponential backoff, not instantly (instant retries refill the full queue).
- Optionally use a profile library (ProfileStore) that does all this.

B22:
Three core instances:
- InputContext: groups actions (e.g. Gameplay, Menu); Enabled, Priority, Sink.
- InputAction: an abstract action (Sprint, Jump); Type (Enum.InputActionType: Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D, ViewportPosition...); events Pressed, Released (Bool only), StateChanged; GetState(); Fire() for simulation.
- InputBinding: maps device input to the action - KeyCode (keyboard/gamepad), UIButton (touch GuiButton), modifiers, Scale/composite directions.
Press signaling: a Bool action fires Pressed when any binding becomes active (Released when it ends); StateChanged fires with the new state for every type; poll GetState() for held input.
Menu precedence: put menu actions in a separate InputContext with a higher Priority than the gameplay/default player-script contexts and Sink = true, so bound inputs are consumed by the menu and not passed to lower-priority contexts (like character movement); enable it when the menu opens (or disable the Gameplay context) and disable it on close. Default player scripts use IAS when Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem is Enabled.
B23:
Roblox's engine UI styling system (CSS-like, StyleSheets):
- StyleSheet: container of rules (usually in ReplicatedStorage).
- StyleRule: has a Selector (class name like "TextButton", tag ".PrimaryButton" via CollectionService tags, "#Name", pseudo-states like ":hover", "::"-phantom modifiers e.g. UICorner, nested child rules) and property overrides set with StyleRule:SetProperty / SetProperties; Priority resolves conflicts.
- StyleLink: placed in a ScreenGui (or other UI root) with StyleLink.StyleSheet = the sheet; that's how styles reach that UI tree - matching descendants get the properties applied automatically and live-update.
- StyleDerive: makes a sheet inherit rules from another (base design system -> theme).
- StyleQuery (conditional, e.g. screen size / preferred input).
Tokens: define attributes on a token StyleSheet (tokens:SetAttribute("Primary", Color3.fromRGB(...))) and reference them in rules as "$Primary"; derive the main sheet from the token sheet. Swapping the token sheet (e.g. dark/light theme with same attribute names) re-themes everything. Don't also set those properties in scripts (conflicts). Studio has a Style Editor (beta).
B24:
Method: facial age estimation (selfie video via the app, processed by a vendor, images deleted after), with ID verification (13+) or parental controls as alternatives/corrections.
Age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, 21+.
Restrictions: chat requires the check; by default users can chat only with their own age group and adjacent groups (e.g. 13-15 with 9-12, 13-15, 16-17). Under-16s can't chat with adults (except Trusted Connections, 13+, who are verified people they know). Under-9 chat is off by default and needs parental consent; Roblox Kids accounts have chat disabled by default. Unchecked users can't use chat.
Rollout: Dec 2025 in Australia, New Zealand, Netherlands; worldwide Jan 2026.
Dev impact: no API exposes a player's age group, and some players' messages are invisible to others; don't make gameplay depend on text chat (use pings, emotes, quick chat).
